organizations.publicNote: German record-manufacturing company. Odeon and Parlophon/Parlophone are represented separately as recording labels rather than as variant corporate names.
Recording label associated with Carl Lindström AG. It is represented separately from the German parent company and from Polskie Zakłady Fonograficzne ‘Odeon’ in Warsaw.

sources.fullCitation: Jan Kiepura with Odeon Künstler-Orchester. “Oh Madonna!” Music by Bronisław Kaper and Walter Jurmann; words by Fritz Rotter and Ernst Marischka; from the sound film Ein Lied für dich. Odeon, shellac 78 rpm, 1933. Internet Archive, George Blood Collection, digitized 78 rpm recording.
sources.title: Oh Madonna! — Odeon
sources.creator: Jan Kiepura; Odeon Künstler-Orchester

sources.shortCitation: BN, Odeon O. 236842 — “Ninon, ach uśmiechnij się!” / “Signorina, signorina” (Kiepura)
sources.fullCitation: “Ninon, ach uśmiechnij się! : z f-mu «Zdobyć cię muszę». Signorina, signorina : z f-mu «Zdobyć cię muszę» / B. Kaper, W. Jurmann ; M. Halicz.” Jan Kiepura, vocal, with the Odeon symphony orchestra. Warsaw: Polskie Zakłady Fonograficzne “Odeon”, [post 1930]. One 78 rpm disc, 25 cm, publisher’s number O. 236842. Biblioteka Narodowa, Magazyn Zbiorów Dźwiękowych i Audiowizualnych, shelfmark Fon.II.11.690; MMS ID 991034500969705066, OCLC 899876292. Language given as Polish, genre as film music. Marcella Halicz is credited “Sł.”, that is for the words.

sources.creator: Jan Kiepura, vocal; Odeon orchestra

sources.shortCitation: Odeon O-11811, “Mein Gorilla hat ’ne Villa im Zoo” (recorded Berlin, 13 February 1933)
sources.fullCitation: Hans Albers with the Odeon-Künstler-Orchester under Otto Dobrindt. “Mein Gorilla hat ’ne Villa im Zoo.” Paso doble. Odeon O-11811, matrix Be 10227-2, 1933. Digital transfer on YouTube; session data consulted in the Odeon label list at musiktiteldb.de.
sources.title: Mein Gorilla hat ’ne Villa im Zoo — Odeon O-11811
sources.creator: Hans Albers, with the Odeon-Künstler-Orchester under Otto Dobrindt
sources.researchNote: The uploader’s description supplies the matrix number; the label is not shown. The recording date, take, studio and April 1933 release follow the Odeon label list at musiktiteldb.de. The companion side, matrix Be 10226, survives in a filmed-label transfer and is documented as part of the same session.

sources.shortCitation: Odeon O-11811 a, “Immer wenn ich glücklich bin” (recorded Berlin, 13 February 1933)
sources.fullCitation: Hans Albers with the Odeon-Künstler-Orchester under Otto Dobrindt. “Immer wenn ich glücklich bin.” Foxtrot from the Boston sound film Heut’ kommt’s drauf an; label credits music to Walter Jurmann and B. Kaper and words to Fritz Rotter. Odeon O-11811 a, matrix Be 10226, 78 rpm, 1933. Filmed-label transfer published on YouTube by Schellackplatte on 21 May 2008.
sources.title: Immer wenn ich glücklich bin — Odeon O-11811 a
sources.creator: Hans Albers; Odeon-Künstler-Orchester, Otto Dobrindt, conductor
sources.researchNote: The recording date of 13 February 1933, Berlin studio 2, and the April 1933 release follow the Odeon label list at musiktiteldb.de. The filmed copy carries a C. A. Klemm dealer sticker and a notice prohibiting radio transmission without permission.

sources.fullCitation: Hans Albers with the Odeon-Künstler-Orchester conducted by O. Dobrindt. “Ich bin der Hans im Glück” / “In 24 Stunden.” Odeon O-11810, shellac, 10-inch, 78 rpm, Germany, 1933. Discogs release 28872088.
sources.title: Ich bin der Hans im Glück / In 24 Stunden — Odeon O-11 810
sources.creator: Hans Albers; Odeon-Künstler-Orchester, O. Dobrindt, conductor
sources.researchNote: Discogs identifies “In 24 Stunden” as matrix Be 10225-2 and the reverse as Be 10224. The recording date, take, Berlin studio and April 1933 release are independently supplied by the Odeon label list at musiktiteldb.de.

sources.shortCitation: Odeon O-11439 a, “Ich weiß ein kleines Café”
sources.fullCitation: Austin Egen, accompanied by the Odeon-Tango-Orchester. “Ich weiß ein kleines Café.” Tango; label credits “Tango (Dr. B. Kaper und Austin Egen)” and “Text: Fritz Rotter”, with the note “Auch als Tanzplatte geeignet”. Odeon O-11439 a, matrix Be 9409, 78 R, B.I.E.M., with “Carl Lindström A.-G.” printed along the foot of the label, n.d. Label filmed in the YouTube upload by Ilja Livschakoff.

sources.fullCitation: Tanz-Orchester Dajos Béla, vocal by Luigi Bernauer, credited on the label as Fred Lustig. “Signorina, ich liebe dich.” Tango; label credits Walter Jurmann, Bronislaw Kaper and Ernst Marischka. Odeon, n.d. Shellac disc, Radiomuseum Hardthausen / Schallarchiv; filmed-label transfer on YouTube.
sources.title: Signorina, ich liebe dich — Odeon
sources.creator: Tanz-Orchester Dajos Béla, Gesang: Luigi Bernauer, auf dem Etikett als Fred Lustig angegeben
sources.researchNote: The uploader associates the side with Hochzeitsreise zu dritt and dates the issue to 1932. The Odeon label list instead identifies the coupling as O-11768, matrix Be 10147, and places it in 1933. Because the filmed label carries no year, the date discrepancy remains unresolved.

sources.shortCitation: Odeon O-11667, “Du liebst mich nicht mehr”
sources.fullCitation: Tanz-Orchester Dajos Béla. “Du liebst mich nicht mehr.” Slow-Fox; label credit “Bob Henders”. Odeon, Katalog-Nr. O-11667, 1932. Digital transfer published on YouTube by Radiomuseum Hardthausen.
sources.title: Du liebst mich nicht mehr — Odeon O-11667
sources.creator: Tanz-Orchester Dajos Béla
sources.researchNote: Uploader-supplied information, not transcribed from the disc label: The upload calls the Odeon issue the first release of the recording and shows a portrait of the bandleader from a Funk-Almanach rather than the disc. The discographic details are taken from the uploader’s description; the label is not shown in the external recording. The Odeon matrix book, indexed at musiktiteldb.de, places the recording in Berlin, Schlesische Straße 26, room 4, on 10 June 1932 under matrix Be 9946, coupled with “Heute Nacht oder nie!”. The label credits the music to Bob Henders alone, the recording name under which Walter Jurmann worked with Kaper.
